subject: HA SLA options + pilot terms / oncall split / credit scaling
messages:
From: Liz Barton <liz@terraops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: HA SLA options + pricing for TerraOps (RFP)

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As promised I'm sending the RFP summary and a couple of must-haves up front so you can steer pricing:

- Two-region footprint (us-west + eu-west) with cross-region failover within 60s.
- Target availability options: 99.9% (standard) vs 99.95% (elevated) — we'd like unit economics for both.
- Critical incidents: 1-hour P1 response, 4-hour P2, plus 24/7 oncall escalation path to an engineer for P1s.
- Requesting a blended monthly credit policy if availability drops below SLA (slab-based).
- We expect steady token volume (gen + embeddings) ~1.2B tokens/month, with spikes during batch jobs.

We also asked procurement to include preferred contract language re: data residency and SOC2 evidence; attaching the RFP PDF. Can you provide:

1) A couple of packaged options (retainer vs a la carte credits) with list prices and discount thresholds for 12/24/36 month commitments.
2) A pilot/POC term (6 weeks) option and any onboarding credits you can offer.
3) How you handle cross-region failover credits and how credits scale with uptime deviation.

Appreciate a strawman by end of week — Arjun (cc) handles procurement.

Thanks,
Liz Barton
Head of Platform, TerraOps
liz@terraops.com
Attachment: TerraOps_RFP_May2028.pdf (pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Barton <liz@terraops.com>
Cc: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@terraops.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: HA SLA options + pricing for TerraOps (RFP)

Hi Liz / Arjun —

Thanks for the clear brief and the RFP PDF. Short version: we can offer both an uptime-tiered retainer and a credit-based pay-as-you-go model. Attached is a first-pass proposal workbook with a pricing matrix and an example credit schedule (redwood_proposal_initial_v1.xlsx). High-level options below so you have something to react to quickly:

Option A — Retainer (predictable):
- 99.9%: Base retainer $22k/mo + usage at $0.0009/token (gen) after committed volume. Includes 8×5 business-hours Tier 1 support; P1 routed to 4hr response with weekday escalation to engineer.
- 99.95%: $35k/mo + $0.00085/token after commit. Includes 24/7 triage + guaranteed 1hr P1 response, direct escalation path (oncall engineer) and quarterly reliability reviews.
- Discounting: 10% off list for 12mo, 15% for 24mo, 20% for 36mo (applied to retainer only).

Option B — Credit model (flexible):
- No retainer; credits purchased monthly to buy priority lanes and uptime credits. Base unit pricing higher but lower upfront.
- Cross-region failover credit: scaled credits paid back if cross-region failover invoked (example: 2% credit of monthly bill for single failover event; increases with duration and frequency).

Pilot proposal (6 weeks):
- Free onboarding credit $12k applied to first invoice + 2 weeks of complimentary high-priority support to validate routing/failover.
- If you convert to retainer within 60 days post-pilot, we’ll apply a conversion credit equal to 25% of onboarding credit.

Two open items we need to align on from your side:
- Expected peak concurrent sessions and % of traffic that must be zero-latency (KV caching expectations).
- Whether TerraOps requires contractual SLA in EU region (data residency/legal clause).

I’ve CC’d Grace (pricing lead) and Jonas (deploy/ops) for their recommendations; Grace — please see the attached workbook and chime in with adjustments to discounts and how we should layer failover credits. Jonas — can you confirm our failover credit examples and how our ops team would operationalize a 60s cross-region failover?

Next steps: once we have the usage profile, we’ll return a clean two-sheet quote (retainer vs credits) and a DocuSign for pilot acceptance.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_proposal_initial_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: HA SLA options + pricing for TerraOps (RFP)

Marcus / Jonas —

Quick pricing POV based on their token volumes and likely negotiating posture: TerraOps looks visa-worthy for a mid-sized commitment with potential scale. My recommended adjustments:

- Anchor the 99.9% at $24k/mo (raise slightly) and hold 99.95% at $34k/mo — that gives us room to concede on discount by 2–5 points without going unprofitable.
- Offer an explicit mixed model: Tiered retainer where the first X tokens are committed, then a lower overage rate + credits for failover. This makes the economics predictable for procurement and gives us a clear uplift path.
- Failover credit formula (proposal):
  - Single failover event (under 30 minutes): 1.5% credit of monthly retainer.
  - Failover event >30 minutes and <3 hours: 5% credit.
  - >3 hours: 12% credit + special review / remediation SLA.
- Pilot: keep onboarding credit $12k but reduce complimentary high-priority support window to 10 business days (we can extend if they convert).
- Escalation staffing: propose a named oncall rotation with one primary Redwood SRE assigned for the first 90 days post-conversion; include in contract as a ‘named resource’ clause for higher-tier.

Jonas — can you confirm operationally: 60s cross-region failover is feasible but depends on app-level connection recovery. We'll provide a runbook and DoS-tested failover procedure; we should not guarantee 60s for long-running streams without additional engineering (we can offer an integration add-on).

If we present that mix, procurement has both predictability and a tangible credit backing. I’ll draft redline language for the credit slabs and named-oncall clause.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Pricing
Redwood Inference
From: Liz Barton <liz@terraops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@terraops.com>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: HA SLA options + pricing for TerraOps (RFP)

Marcus —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and thanks Grace for the clarity. A few follow-ups from procurement and platform:

1) We prefer the mixed-retainer you outlined (predictable + overage), but procurement asks for a 15% discount on the 24mo commit instead of 15% off retainer only — they want the conversion credit applied against total spend in year 1. Will Redwood agree to this if we commit to 24 months and provide PoC acceptance criteria?

2) The failover credit slabs look reasonable. We’d like the >3 hours slab to include a refund credit that scales with customer impact score (we'll provide a brief impact table).

3) Pilot: we accept the $12k onboarding credit, but ask that the 10 business day complimentary high-priority support be extended to 14 calendar days (to align with our weekend tests). If we convert to retainer within 60 days, TerraOps requests a one-time additional operational credit equal to 1 month of retainer.

4) On the named-oncall clause — we appreciate that for the first 90 days. Post-conversion, can we request an option to purchase extended named coverage as an add-on for months 4–12 at a fixed rate?

If you can sign these points off in writing, procurement will prepare a term sheet and we'll send back our standard redlines. Also please send a DocuSign pilot acceptance when you confirm the 14-day support window.

Best,
Liz Barton
Head of Platform, TerraOps
